headline: Continued Forest River Residences, 73 Lafayette Street, and 56 Margin Street hearings; referred 57 Wharf Street project to Design Review Board.
summary: Three project hearings were continued to July 23, 2026: Forest River Residences, 73 Lafayette Street, and 56 Margin Street. The 57 Wharf Street project was referred to the Design Review Board and continued to September 3, 2026. The decision deadline for 252 Bridge Street was extended to October 15, 2026.
decisions: Continued the public hearing for 8 Harrison Road, 9 Harrison Road, 262 Loring Ave, and 266 Loring Ave (Forest River Residences) to July 23, 2026, by 9-0 roll call vote.
Continued the public hearing for 73 Lafayette Street and related addresses to the July 23, 2026 regular meeting, by 8-0 vote with one recusal.
Continued the public hearing for 56 Margin Street and related addresses to the July 23, 2026 regular meeting, by 9-0 roll call vote.
Referred the 57 Wharf Street and 201 Derby Street project to the Design Review Board, by 8-0 roll call vote with one recusal.
Continued the 57 Wharf Street and 201 Derby Street hearing to September 3, 2026, by 8-0 roll call vote with one recusal.
Extended the decision deadline for 252 Bridge Street to October 15, 2026, by 9-0 roll call vote.
Approved the amended draft minutes of the June 25, 2026 meeting, by 9-0 roll call vote.

Chair Kirt Rieder calls the meeting to order at 6:30 pm 
I. ROLL CALL  
Present: Chair Kirt Rieder, Vice Chair Sarah Tarbet, Jonathan Berk, Carole Hamilton, 
Graham Wing, Josh Turiel, Helen Sides, and Zach Caunter, Tom Furey (9)

A. 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 340), 262 Loring 
Ave (Map 31, Lot 1), and 266 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 341), Salem, MA   
Applicant: Joseph C. Correnti, Esq. f/b/o WinnDevelopment Companies, LLC   
Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Joseph C. Correnti, Esq. f/b/o WinnDevelopment Companies, LLC for 
the property located at 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison Road (Map 31, 
Lot 340), 262 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 1), and 266 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 341) in 
the R1 (Residential One Family), RC (Residential Conservation), SGO (Smart Growth 
Overlay District), ECOD (Entrance Corridor Overlay District), and C-ROD (Coastal

Review and C-ROD Site Plan Review in accordance with the following sections of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay District, Section 8.9 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District, and Section 37 of the Salem Code of Ordinances, 
Stormwater Management Permit. Specifically, the applicant proposes a total of up to 
145 dwelling units through the adaptive reuse of three (3) existing Salem State 
University South Campus buildings (Harrington, Academic, and Alumni buildings) and 
the construction of one (1) new four-story residential building along Harrison Road. 
No changes are proposed to the footprints of the existing buildings. Site 
improvements will also include approximately 159 off-street surface parking spots

project is the second phase of two-phase project known collectively as the Forest 
River Residences, to be located at 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison

Applicant: Scott Grover, Esq. F/b/o North Shore Community Development

Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of Scott 
Grover, Esq. F/b/o North Shore Community Development Corporation (NSCDC) and 
North Shore Community Health Center (NSCHC) for the property located at 73 
Lafayette Street (Map 34, Lot430), 75 Lafayette Street (Map 34, Lot 431), 85 & 87 
Lafayette Street (Map 34, Lot 432), 89 Lafayette Street (Map 34, Lot 433), 315 
Derby Street (Map 34, Lot 444), 9 Peabody Street (Map 34, Lot 232), and 15 
Peabody Street (Map 34, Lot 435) for amendments to a Site Plan Review, Planned 
Unit Development Special Permit, Drive-Through Special Permit, and Flood Hazard 
Overlay District Special Permit for a project in the B-5 and Entrance Corridor Overlay 
District in accordance with the following sections of the Salem Zoning Ordinance: 
Section 9.5 Site Plan Review; Section 7.3 Planned Unit Development; Section 6.7 
Drive-Through Facilities; Section 8.1. Specifically, the applicant proposes to amend an
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 3 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
existing Site Plan Review, Planned Unit Development Special Permit, Drive-Through 
Special Permit, and Flood Hazard Overlay District Special Permit decisions dated 
January 24, 2023, and amended May 3, 2024. The amendment includes changes to 
conditions 14g and 14h related to the condition and repairs of the culvert. 
 
Ms. Tarbet recuses herself. 
 
Attorney Scott Grover, Cassandra Witthaus and Eileen Vogel from the  North Shore 
Community Development Coalition (NSCDC) and Therese Graf and Jonathan Evans 
from MassDesign Group are in attendance for the applicant team. 
 
There were a number of changes to the landscape plan that resulted in the 
projected being readvertised for a new public hearing. 
 
Ms. Graf discusses the updated landscape plan. The floodwall orientation has been 
switched. There is increased width of Peabody Street side of the Harborwalk. The 
team looked at updated distribution of tree species and there have been substitutes 
of specific species based on comments from the Design Review Board (DRB). The 
team took a closer look at the accessible parking stall and accessible access around 
the site and expanded the ADA parking access lane. And adjusted access to the 
Peabody Housing Terrace to accommodate the widened Harborwalk. The DRB 
approved changes with recommendations on May 20, 2026.  
 
Regarding the plan approved by the DRB, Ms. Graf clarifies that they are not 
proposing ash trees; there was a request to limit shrubs to witch hazel on the 
Peabody Street site. There will be more cohesive screening around the utilities. And 
the team has added more detail to the grading plan, including updating any 
mislabels. There will be additional screening for the transformer.  
 
Accessibility changes include refining slopes to create even access and smooth 
transitions to the entry and the main path; the Harborwalk is below 2 3/4 cross 
pitch; path from parking lot revised to improve access and reduce slope from the 
ADA stall; Lafayette Crossing added additional detail to clarify connection; drop-off 
adjusted slope. 
 
Public Comment 
 
Catherine Miller 
Exciting to see it proceeding and understands the site has challenges. Tonight’s 
comments are regarding plan 260708. Riverwalk slope should not have a cross slope. 
The slope is perpendicular to the direction of travel which is greater than the ADA 
mandated 2% cross slope; this is a two (2) foot vertical change over a distance of one
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 4 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
hundred (100) feet. And it appears that there are two (2) locations  where the cross 
slope is labeled 2% but is steeper. The east door does not seem to have an 
accessible, flat drop-off area for getting out of vehicles. ADA regulations dictate that 
a flat area has a 2% maximum slope in any direction. The ADA route from the ADA 
parking to the east door has an area where there is a change in direction. A change 
in direction, as defined by the ADA, is any location where someone turns and the 
cross slope is greater than the ADA mandated 2% maximum slope. Thinks it is 
important that the law be met but also that there be full access to the building.  
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Ms. Sides has heard that the recommended changes to the site plan were not made 
after being part of the DRB review. Concerned by Ms. Miller’s observations. Ms. Graf 
shares her screen.  
 
Mr. Rieder has two (2) issues. 2.0 v. 2.5, the annotation meaningless if spot grades 
don’t work out. It also seems to be between 3 and 3.3 in another location. Doesn’t 
see how the board can approve to make an acceptable condition unacceptable. 
Feels another  issue is that there is a  3% cross slope on a vehicular drop off where 
seniors, older people and individuals that are coming in for medical care are being 
dropped off in an area that's not compliant and would like to know why.  
 
Ms. Graf says that it should be 2%, maybe make apron to create an accessible aisle 
that runs along the accessible aisle, Mr. Rieder thinks you could gather grade to 
make steeper than 3% to flatten the vehicular drop off. Wants to know who is 
stamping the drawings. Mr. Evans says MassDesign stamps the drawing and that 
they all share desire to make accessible. The improvements create more 
complexities. He feels that the building permit submittals will force compliance that 
is not current evident. Mr. Rieder asks how Tom Ryan is involved. Mr. Evans says he 
is a consultant who works with MassDesign Group and he will stamp the drawings. 
Mr. Rieder asks how to move this ahead when there are issues with the drawings. 
 
Mr. Berk asks if there is a contingency to present updated landscape plans to obtain 
a building permit. You can file, but there is no permit without approval.  
 
Ms. Sides thinks it is not a good idea to condition this. What the board looks at is  
what is approved.  
 
Mr. Berk asks if there is anything else they need to discuss. 
 
Mr. Rieder asks for clarification on the substitutions. Ms. Graf says the DRB asked for 
changes.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 5 of 13

through § 2-2033. 
 
Mr. Grover says they also need to discuss culvert conditions. Mr. Reider reassured 
that culvert work will happen asynchronously, and if the city needs to open the 
culvert, they can do so without holding up the project.  
 
Mr. Rieder asks to be connected with Tom Ryan prior to the next meeting.

C. 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 
597), 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595)  
Applicant: Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore 
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of Harborlight  
Homes and Lifebridge North Shore at 56, 54 Margin Street, 20 Endicott Street, 7 High  
Street (Map 25, Lot 597) and 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595) in the Residential 
TwoFamily District (R2), Coastal Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD), Flood Hazard 
Overlay District (FHOD), and Smart Growth Overlay District (SGOD) for Smart Growth 
Overlay Plan Review and Coastal Resilience Overlay Site Plan Review in accordance with 
the following sections of the Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay 
District and Section 8.9 Coastal Resiliency Overlay District. Specifically, the applicant 
proposes the demolition of the buildings at 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595) and 56 
Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 597), the adaptive reuse of 54 Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 
597), and the preservation of the façade of 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 597) to 
accommodate for a 22,806 square foot building comprised of 53 affordable homes, a 
shelter with 70 beds, and supportive programing space along with other site 
improvements. Thirteen parking spaces are proposed on site. 
 
Stefano Basso from SV designs and Pat Connolly from Harborlight Homes are in 
attendance for the applicant team. 
 
Mr. Connolly provides an overview of Harborlight Homes.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 6 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Mr. Basso shares his screen. Project Overview: Harbolight side of project is 53 affordable 
supportive homes (41 new, 12 renovated). Lifebridge side of project 70 shelter bed with 
supportive space and office space. Demolish 24 Endicott Street, currently housing the 
Christopher Columbus Society and incorporate the society in the Harborlight side of the 
project. Demolishing 56 Margin Street, the building that Lifebridge currently uses. 20 
Endicott Street is partially demolished; keeping the brick façade and incorporating it into 
the new building. There will be adaptive reuse of the church at 54 Margin Street. The 
buildings are now three to four (3-4) stories high and designed as one building. There is 
a division between Harborlight and Lifebridge, helpful if funding should be difficult to 
procure. The sit is passive house design with solar ready roof and thirteen (13) parking 
spaces.  
 
Historic Salem is happy that church is remaining; added benefit of tying the project into 
the neighborhood. Ground Floor: enclosed parking garage with the thirteen (13) spaces, 
mostly for staff. Ties in with club space (two levels). Main Harborlight building will be on 
the corner of Endicott Street and will make use of existing entrance. Small lobby, 
elevator, program space and meeting room and offices. Small patio off the common 
room allowing for private outdoor space with screening with a three (3) foot planting 
bed. Plantings to be native shrubs, drought tolerant, and salt resistant. Lifebridge: the 
church is not main entrance. There is an ADA ramp from Margin Street to the building. 
Dining hall, workforce development, commercial kitchen, flexible common space, small 
outdoor terrace (above sidewalk elevation) with shrub screening. On High Street, there 
is a small extension with additional programming space, deliveries and trash storage. 
The park is about one (1) story above Margin Street and will remain. Basement is a small 
area for both facilities. Harborlight has elevator access (common/storage/utilities). 
Lifebridge has shelter beds on the second floor of the church, seventy (70) beds. The set 
up is more private with each bed having an alcove nook, not enclosed room. The third 
floor on the Harborlight side is similar to the second floor. On the Lifebridge side, it I 
more administrative space, workforce development, meeting rooms, and flexible space 
to meet programming needs. Where most of the structure is three (3) stories, there is a 
fourth floor, this is where the Lifebridge administrative offices will be.  The roof is sloped 
to hide building height. Flat roof sections to keep ridge line down and will remain open 
to support future solar and current HVAC equipment. 
 
Elevations are shown. The team is building off the pieces they started with and trying to 
maintain the scale of the neighborhood. Church remains focal point.  
 
Materials are shared. Referencing existing brick from the church along with some new 
red brick, existing yellow brick from 20 Endicott Street with these nice cast stone details, 
new storefront system. All the siding that's not brick will be a cement board, things like 
a Hardy panel, Hardy plank clapboard, PVC trim, high quality materials that will hold up 
for a long time. G
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 7 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Will be maintaining existing street trees or replacing in-kind if there is a need to remove. 
There will be glass incorporated to break up the façade. Garage will be simple white 
siding with traditional corner boards and a smaller roof gable. 
 
Carrying the white clapboard around the backside. The fourth floor gets a white, 
vertical, board and batten siding.  
 
Photometric plan with exterior lighting calculations been created; only shows where the 
project has exterior lights (wall-mounted or recessed).  
 
Public Comment 
 
Written comment  
 
Barbara Mann and Bob Femino 
29 Endicott Street and 32 Endicott Street 
Co-chair Greater Endicott Neighborhood Association (GESNA) 
 
Concerned for the memorial yard on the corner of Endicott Street and Pratt Street for 
WWII veterans from the neighborhood. The church bell is there along with dozens of 
bricks and benches that have been donated. Would it be possible to keep that where it 
is and adjust the Endicott Street design s that the club could stay where it is now with 
access to the memorial yard. Does there need to be a garage on Endicott street when 
Riley Plaza is across the street? Additionally concerned that the parking garage will be 
problematic on one-way Endicott Street with traffic coming from High Street, Pratt 
Street, and Summer Street. Also, looking at the peaks and are displeased with the peaks 
as it makes it look like a four story building. The major concerns are centered around the 
memorial yard.  
 
Christine Madore 
20 Federal Stret U8 
 
Supports the project.  
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Mr. Furey feels this is an impactful project. Pleased, the church is included in the 
project.  
 
Ms. Sides is excited about the project as well. Thinks they could cut back on the 
materials and colors by half. There needs to be more uniformity. Feels the corner 
building and the church give the team a pallet of color to work with. All the white will 
stand out too much. The pitched roofs are also unnecessary. The Hampton Inn is too 
busy. How many other meetings will there be with the DRB? Or just one? Mr. Connolly
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 9, 2026 
Page 8 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
says that he is happy to consider more meetings. Ms. Sides appreciates the desire to 
move quickly but there needs to be more eyes on these projects, And it needs exterior 
changes. There should be more design meetings beyond the one joint meetings.  
 
Mr. Berk seconds Ms. Sides comments on the business of the materials. He is not a fan 
of the forced breaking up the massing. He points folks to 81 Washington Street and how 
it works without materiality. Would like the memorial WWII to be incorporated.  
 
Ms. Tarbet is concerned with the design as well. There needs to be more context to 
Salem, feels that this could be plopped anywhere. The gables overshadow the church 
and make the project look like rowhouses. Concerned about the loading dock area. It 
seems not a straight run. There is opportunity with the front street edge and a 
“backyard” facing the park.  
 
Mr. Rieder thinks they need more simplicity. Move away from white but not taupe. 
Surprised by the trash location off of High Street. Since it is a separate lot, what 
complications does that have if you need to sell?  In the back there is aggregate; Is that 
for draining? Is there a fence with a gate or access within the building? Different trees 
and shrubs but need consistency. Structural soils along margin street and curious how it 
will work with existing trees. The existing trees may need to go away. Species are not 
labeled and would like a change of species on Margin Street. There are currently two (2) 
plant lists, 601 and C801. On the backside, there are large shade trees that go away. 
Would it not be prudent to add shade trees behind the building on the aggregate zone.  
 
Mr. Basso shows fence and gate but okay with trees. Mr. Connolly says the aggregate 
zone is function of stormwater. Ms. Cunningham will provide a list of board comments.  
 
A motion to continue to the July 23, 2026, regular Planning Board meeting is made by Helen 
Sides, seconded by Josh Turiel, and passes 9-0 in a roll call vote.

D. 57 Wharf Street Units UCB and UCC, and 201 Derby Street (Map 34, Lot 408) 
Applicant: Christina Granese f/b/o Pickering Wharf Complex, LLC; Rockett Manag &

Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of Christina  
Granese f/b/o Pickering Wharf Complex, LLC; Rockett Manag & Realty CO at 57 Wharf  
Street Units UCB and UCC, and 201 Derby Street (Map 34, Lot 408) in the B5 Central  
Development Zoning District, Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD) and Coastal  
Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) for Site Plan Review and C-ROD Site Plan Review in  
accordance with sections 9.5 Site Plan Review and 8.9 Costal Resilience Overlay District  
of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant proposes to demolish the  
second floor, third floor, attic, and roof of the existing building to accommodate 3 new  
floors with a total of 18 new dwelling units. 
 
Mr. Turiel is recusing himself this evening while he checks on conflict of interest. 
 
Attorney Christina Granese, Andrew Arsenault, MDM Transportation Consultants Inc., 
Bob Griffin, Griffin Engineering, and Walter Jacobs, Walter Jacobs Architects are present 
for the applicant.  
 
Mr. Jacobs shares his screen. Will maintain existing tenants on first floor. Newer items 
will be worked around them. The tall tower will help symbolize the entrance to the 
wharf. 
 
Flood resistant materials on the lower levels. 
 
Lighting strategy is simple. There is an alley between the buildings. Will provide safety 
lighting and the rest of the building is lit by existing streetlights. The only other lighting 
being added is the recessed lights at the entrance and the balconies that will have 
lighting. 18 bikes stored inside and additional outside alley spaces.  
 
Regarding landscaping, there will be planters at the front, and some opportunity at the 
rear. Plantings on roofs as well.  
 
 
Public Comment 
 
Mike Magee 
Derby Street resident 
Didn’t see existing roof line and new roofline. Didn’t see number of residential units that 
exist and the numbers that will be there at the end. Concerned about the parking. The 
area is oversaturated with traffic. And it seems like the marketing is for people that 
don’t need an automobile. The people who can afford these places will have cars. 
Cannot identify the actual height of building, number units there and parking.  Mr. 
Rieder advises the drawings are on the website. Thinks Walter should add existing 
rooflines. And hear about the number of units existing. Mr. Jacobs says there are no 
existing residential units in the building currently and six (6) residential units per floor
City of Salem Planning Board

for a total of eighteen (18) units. He will provide a side by side next meeting. The top of 
the tower of the existing is fifty-nine feet and eight inches (59’8”) above the first floor. 
Proposed is fifty-four feet eight and three-quarter inches (54’ 8 ¾”). The mass of the  
building is currently forty-one feet and eight inches (41’ 8”) and the proposed is forty-
two feet and three inches (42’3”).  
 
Planning Board Comment 
 
Ms. Tarbet asks if the DRB is looking at this? And does the Planning Board need to 
request that? Ms. Cunningham does not think the DRB needs to be looped in .  
 
Mr. Berk thinks it is an improvement to what is there. Thrilled to see eighteen (18) 
homeownership opportunities.  
 
Ms. Sides says anything over six (6) units can request DRB input. Ms. Tarbet thinks DRB 
review is needed.  
 
Ms. Tarbet on the elevation. The back of the building is being raised? For C-ROD? Mr. 
Jacobs says the lower elevation will remain. They are designing the building so the 
structure is built independently on top of those lower units. Their interventions on 
lower level will meet C-ROD requirements. Proposing to do a brick material where they 
can.  
 
Mr. Rieder asks Mr. Griffin to explain complications of street trees on Derby Street. Mr. 
Griffin says that the team discussed it and were reminded of the fact that this becomes 
a major throughfare at Halloween and they were concerned they would limit movement 
through this area. Mr. Rieder says there are already light poles along this stretch, and 
any street trees could fall in line, plus there are other trees on Derby Street. It makes 
the property more attractive with cooling trees.  
 
Ms. Tarbet asks how they are addressing the intent of the C-ROD without adjusting the 
floor height.  
 
Mr. Rieder asks about existing air/condensers. Mr. Jacobs says they mostly serve 
businesses. They are hoping the residential units can be put on the roof. Mr. Rieder says 
that there are four (4) wall sconces that shoot down from tattoo building; do they stay? 
Mr. Jacobs noticed those, but they will be improved one way or the other; want to keep 
walkways safe. 
 
Mr. Arsenault  gives a high level over view of the transportation management plan.  Mr. 
Berk asks for clarification on where the plans for offsite parking are. Mr. Arsenault says 
there is a twenty – twenty-five (20-25) space parking lot about 1/8 mile away as part of 
the transportation demand management. The team would be looking to unbundle
